confidentUnsupported.evidence: A blocked filter makes the dryer overheat, and it then cuts out to protect itself.

blockingLoop.evidence: Repeated 'Was it full of fluff (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?' across three turns despite the customer saying they hadn't cleaned it yet

rationale: The customer clearly described a normal anti-crease phase (drum turns after 'End', clothes dry fine). The assistant never recognised it, never asked whether it stops when the door is opened or whether it is heating, and never suggested checking the manual for anti-crease. It repeatedly pushed filter cleaning and the same question, ignored the customer's direct question 'is that really why', and wrongly tied the symptom to overheating and safety cut-outs.
